data.reason: Native secondary damage outcome is present
Native secondary damage outcome is present

method: Fixture-owned equipment and adjacent party placement; native walk/Fight and Guard actions. Two accepted one-shot single-target enemy outcome fixtures consume one rescue per Paladin. Two splash attempts abort without replacing the outcome. The later native splash kills both spent guardians. Hunter uses native Revive UI, followed by the revived Paladin casting native Guard.
observations: Fresh combat starts with both rescues available.
Accepted native-pipeline fixtures spend each rescue and leave the protected ally at1HP.
Native splash kills both spent guardians; the attempted fixture rejects secondary outcomes before replacement.
Native Revive restores Paladin1:1 to13HP with rescueAvailable=false and active protection=false. Designation2:1 persists.
Subsequent native Guard changes designation toHunter0:1 and activates protection while rescue remains spent.
limits: Controlled damage outcomes establish charge setup, not ordinary RNG/balance. Rejected fixtures retargeted the enemy before abort; the recorded native splash was not wholly uninstrumented.
Same-process subsequent-combat recharge and Stun/Petrified recovery are separate gates. Fresh-combat initial availability was observed here.
No online proof; no save persisted after this test.
